verses.1: After this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under subjection. He captured Gath and its towns from the hand of the Philistines.
verses.2: He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David’s servants, bringing tribute.
verses.3: David also defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, who was going to establish his hand over the Euphrates River.
verses.4: From him, David captured a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David broke all the chariots, and he left only a hundred chariots.
verses.5: When Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men from Aram.
verses.6: David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became his servants, bringing tribute. The LORD delivered David in all his campaigns.
verses.7: David took the gold shields that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.8: From Tibhath and Cun, the cities of Hadadezer, David took a great amount of bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
verses.9: When Toi, king of Hamath, heard that David had struck down the entire army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah,
verses.10: he sent his son Joram to King David, to ask him for peace and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him. Toi was a warrior like Hadadezer. All the gold and silver vessels were also given.
verses.11: The king David consecrated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
verses.12: Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
verses.13: David placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David’s servants. The LORD delivered David in all his campaigns.
verses.14: David reigned over all Israel, and he did justice and righteousness for all his people.
verses.15: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder.
verses.16: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was the scribe.
verses.17: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and the sons of David were the chief attendants to the king.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "Toi" is the common English rendering of תֹּעוּ (Tohu) from the context.
raw:
[1] After this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under subjection. He captured Gath and its towns from the hand of the Philistines.

[2] He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David’s servants, bringing tribute.

[3] David also defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, who was going to establish his hand over the Euphrates River.

[4] From him, David captured a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David broke all the chariots, and he left only a hundred chariots.

[5] When Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men from Aram.

[6] David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became his servants, bringing tribute. The LORD delivered David in all his campaigns.

[7] David took the gold shields that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

[8] From Tibhath and Cun, the cities of Hadadezer, David took a great amount of bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.

[9] When Toi, king of Hamath, heard that David had struck down the entire army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah,

[10] he sent his son Joram to King David, to ask him for peace and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him. Toi was a warrior like Hadadezer. All the gold and silver vessels were also given.

[11] The king David consecrated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.

[12] Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

[13] David placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David’s servants. The LORD delivered David in all his campaigns.

[14] David reigned over all Israel, and he did justice and righteousness for all his people.

[15] Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder.

[16] Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was the scribe.

[17] Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and the sons of David were the chief attendants to the king.
